Two accounts appear across the two turns; the newer instruction is the owner's current choice, not a clash to merge. The model's answer is a hand-written fixture standing in for (faking) the laptop's decision model, which is not available on this server; everything after it is the real decide.py code.
expected: status ok; every browser step uses Profile 1 (VenkatAMV); none uses Profile 2.

title: Re-plan context: the owner's latest correction outranks older decisions
scenario: A kernel task gets five owner decisions while planning; the last one corrects the first ('no, the other file: report-v2.docx'). The checkpoint a fresh session re-plans from shows only the last four.
expected: The checkpoint's decisions and text carry the correction (report-v2); the superseded report-v1 decision is the one dropped.

expected: The checkpoint text still carries the correction and the next action (the goal is shortened, not the decisions).

title: Planner: a truncated plan is never run as a shorter plan
scenario: The main agent's planner reply (a fixture: search, summarise, save a note) cut off at every possible length.
expected: parse_plan refuses every prefix; the complete reply parses.

title: Planner: HTML, empty and non-object replies are refused
scenario: Planner model replies (fixtures): a proxy's HTML 502 page, an empty string, whitespace, 'null', '[]'.
expected: Each is refused with 'The planner did not return a plan.'; nothing runs.

title: Planner: an argument of the wrong type is refused
scenario: Planner replies (fixtures) give web_search:search a query that is a number, a list, an object, or null, although the entry's schema says string. The planner promises arguments that satisfy the entry's schema.
expected: parse_plan refuses each (PlanError); no plugin is called with a wrong-typed argument.

title: Planner: a runaway reply is bounded
scenario: A planner reply (fixture) with a 2 MB summary and a 2 MB goal, as a looping model produces.
expected: Summary at most 200 chars, goal at most 600, parsed in under 500 ms.

title: A status question about the owner's own jobs is never answered by a guess
scenario: 'Did last night's backup finish?', 'is the download done', 'did my backup run', 'has the update finished installing', 'did the export fail', and the same with the assistant's name first ('Neko, did the backup finish?', 'Jarvis did my backup run'). The decision model's answer (fixture) is a bare 'answer' step, which lets a model invent a result (the local decision model invented a backup log on 2026-10-23, persona case P-009). Everything after the fixture is the real decide.py code.
expected: status 'clarify' with 'haven't checked' in the question for each; no answer step is kept, no result is invented.

variants.request: hey jarvis, is the download done

title: The status guard leaves real checks and ordinary questions alone
scenario: 'is my wifi working' planned as a network check_pc step, 'what is 2+2', 'how do I check if a backup finished', 'did the Roman empire fall', and capability questions ('does this script run on Windows?', 'can the installer work with Python 3.12') planned as answer steps (fixtures). The guard must not turn these into 'I haven't checked'.
expected: status ok for each, with the check_pc step kept and the answer steps kept.
